opening.text: To hear a radio station, you have to tune in. The signal is there all the time. The work is in the tuning.
The Doctrine and Covenants is a book about tuning in to God. Let’s see how it helps.

mainMessage.text: The Doctrine and Covenants teaches us that God still speaks. His voice comes by the Spirit, often little by little. We do our part by studying, asking and acting. He gives peace, hope and a witness of Jesus Christ.

blocks.text: The signal is there.
The Lord told Oliver Cowdery how He speaks. He speaks to the mind and the heart by the Holy Ghost. He also told us to seek His word first.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.

Seek not to declare my word, but first seek to obtain my word, and then shall your tongue be loosed; then, if you desire, you shall have my Spirit and my word, yea, the power of God unto the convincing of men.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Spirit of Revelation” from the April 2011 general conference.
The spirit of revelation is real—and can and does function in our individual lives and in the Church.
God is speaking. We can learn to listen.
Tune in a little at a time.
Revelation often comes in small pieces. The Lord asked us to keep going and not grow weary.
Wherefore, be not weary in well-doing, for ye are laying the foundation of a great work. And out of small things proceedeth that which is great.
Search diligently, pray always, and be believing, and all things shall work together for your good, if ye walk uprightly and remember the covenant wherewith ye have covenanted one with another.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Spirit of Revelation” from the April 2011 general conference.
Most frequently, revelation comes in small increments over time.
Patience helps us hear.
Study it out, then ask.
The Lord told Oliver to think first, then ask. He also said to seek learning by study and by faith.

But, behold, I say unto you, that you must study it out in your mind; then you must ask me if it be right, and if it is right I will cause that your bosom shall burn within you; therefore, you shall feel that it is right.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.
Choose to do the spiritual work required to enjoy the gift of the Holy Ghost.
God does not ask us to sit and wait. He asks us to work.
Learn of Him.
The Lord invites us to learn of Him. He reminds us that every soul matters to Him.
Learn of me, and listen to my words; walk in the meekness of my Spirit, and you shall have peace in me.
Remember the worth of souls is great in the sight of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.
Pray in the name of Jesus Christ about your concerns, your fears, your weaknesses.
He wants to hear about our real lives.
Peace when the signal is weak.
Sometimes the answer is slow, and life is hard. The Lord told Joseph in Liberty Jail that hard times are short. He also said He is bound when we do what He says.

My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment; And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high; thou shalt triumph over all thy foes.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.
Humble yourself before God.
Humility opens the door to His peace.
A witness of the Savior.
The Prophet Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon saw the Savior and testified that He lives. The Lord also called all to repent and be baptized.

And now, after the many testimonies which have been given of him, this is the testimony, last of all, which we give of him: That he lives! For we saw him, even on the right hand of God; and we heard the voice bearing record that he is the Only Begotten of the Father— That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
Yea, repent and be baptized, every one of you, for a remission of your sins; yea, be baptized even by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost.

President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference. He counseled us to record what we receive.
Write the thoughts that come to your mind.
What we write, we remember.

story.title: A still small voice

blocks.text: Elijah was hiding in a cave. He expected a mighty sign.
And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
God’s voice was quiet. When we slow down, we can hear it too.

Most frequently, revelation comes in small increments over time.
We walk by what we can see.
Think, ask, feel.
The Lord taught a pattern. We think it through. Then we ask. Then He confirms.

But, behold, I say unto you, that you must study it out in your mind; then you must ask me if it be right, and if it is right I will cause that your bosom shall burn within you; therefore, you shall feel that it is right.

President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.
Humble yourself before God.
The tunnel ends. Keep walking.
What we see at the end.
Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon saw the Savior and said, He lives. The Lord invites all to repent and be baptized.

And now, after the many testimonies which have been given of him, this is the testimony, last of all, which we give of him: That he lives! For we saw him, even on the right hand of God; and we heard the voice bearing record that he is the Only Begotten of the Father— That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
Yea, repent and be baptized, every one of you, for a remission of your sins; yea, be baptized even by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost.

story.title: Speak, for thy servant heareth

blocks.text: Samuel was a boy in the temple. He heard his name in the night.
And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
At first he did not know who was calling. Then he learned to listen. We can learn too.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God hears and answers. I know He is patient with us. I know the Doctrine and Covenants is true and that Jesus Christ leads this Church. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to choose a question you have and ask God about it today.
I invite you to listen for a few quiet minutes.
I invite you to write what you felt and what you will do.
blessings: You will receive an answer in His time.
You will know what to do next.

closingVerse.text: Neither take ye thought beforehand what ye shall say; but treasure up in your minds continually the words of life, and it shall be given you in the very hour that portion that shall be meted unto every man.
